# **DEEP CASE DOSSIER: THE EVOLUTION OF BEHAVIORAL CONTROL NETWORKS**

## **SECTION I: ORIGIN SITES AND ORGANIC SERVO-LINKAGES (1943–1953)**

**ARTIFACT 01-A** **PROVENANCE:** University of Minnesota (Psychology/behavioral research context), Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA (44.9739, \-93.2277) **DATE:** December 14, 1943 **TYPE:** Laboratory Notes / Experimental Setup Log (Fragment 4A) **CONTENTS:** The Pelican glide bomb steering problem, characterized by the abysmal accuracy of high-altitude bombing, requires a functional, biological guidance system capable of tracking a target with zero-lag responsiveness.1 The vacuum-tube electronics supplied by the National Defense Research Committee (NDRC) are highly sensitive to countermeasures and drift, often losing lock in cluttered environments. To circumvent this, we have strapped three trained pigeons into custom-fitted canvas harnesses located directly behind a translucent screen within the specialized nose cone.1

A pneumatic pickup system, designed to give a graded signal, serves as the primary servo link.2 A specially ground lens positioned at the front of the missile projects the surrounding physical area onto the screen.3 Conditioning is strictly operant. Food is dispensed mechanically upon the successful peck-tracking of the target image. As the bomb deviates in flight, the target image drifts to the screen's outer portion. The bird's pecks on the individual conductive discs activate the servo link, creating a continuous feedback loop that corrects the trajectory.2 Laboratory trials indicate the organism can track a target moving at simulated speeds exceeding 600 miles per hour, demonstrating an uncanny ability to ignore deliberately introduced light flashes and smoke.1 The shaping process, refined during the preliminary studies at the General Mills flour mill, proves that behavior can be constructed entirely through environmental contingencies.2

**ARTIFACT 01-B** **PROVENANCE:** Harvard University Archives / Pusey Library, Cambridge, Massachusetts, USA (42.3744, \-71.1169) **DATE:** March 2, 1944 **TYPE:** Manuscript Draft (B.F. Skinner) **CONTENTS:** The organism is a self-contained computational matrix. We do not need to understand the physiological interior; we only need to manage the schedule of reinforcement. The military engineers fail to grasp that the pigeon is not a pilot, but an organic switch operating on a variable-ratio schedule. We have coated the glass screen with stannic oxide to make it electrically conducting.3 The beak strikes the glass, completing the circuit. The conductive gold leaf translates these pecks into electrical signals that move the missile's fins, adjusting the flight path in real-time.1 The organism is no longer a separate entity from the machine; it is a wetware component fused into the pneumatic pickup system.

**ARTIFACT 01-D** **PROVENANCE:** The Pentagon, Arlington, Virginia, USA (38.8719, \-77.0563) **DATE:** October 8, 1944 **TYPE:** Memorandum of Termination, National Defense Research Committee (NDRC) **CONTENTS:** Effective immediately, the funding allocation of $25,000 for Project Pigeon is hereby revoked.1 High-ranking military officials found the idea of a bird-brained bomb humiliating and absurd, despite laboratory proofs.1 The system is considered too eccentric and impractical.3

The failure of the system is not biological, but bureaucratic. It is primarily attributed to the strict compartmentalization of information; engineers at General Mills were denied access to critical aerodynamic details of the Pelican steering mechanism, resulting in a fundamentally inadequate servomechanism.2 Furthermore, OSRD physicists and engineers simply refuse to trust an organic entity with the task of guiding precision ordnance.2 However, the committee recommends that the "organic system of control" should be examined in the future, as the precision of the variable-ratio reinforcement model presents clear utility for other autonomous systems.2

**ARTIFACT 01-E** **PROVENANCE:** Naval Research Laboratory, Washington, DC, USA (38.8200, \-77.0189) **DATE:** November 25, 1959 **TYPE:** Declassified Technical Report Extract (Retrospective on 1948–1953 tests) **CONTENTS:** Project Orcon (Organic Control) revived the 1943 paradigm under the direction of Dr. F.V. Taylor.3 The primary motivation was the ease with which current electronic homing systems were being countermeasured; animals presented a potential jam-proof control element.3 Pigeons were selected because they were light, easily obtainable, and highly adaptable to operant frameworks.3

Trainee subjects began in the primary trainer pecking at slowly moving target images photographed in color by a jet plane making picture-taking dives at a destroyer and a freighter in the open sea.3

| Performance Metric | Recorded System Value | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Simulated Missile Speed | \~400 mph 3 | Emulated via projection speed |
| Target Jitter Rate | 5 inches per second 3 |  |
| Continuous Tracking Duration | 80 seconds 3 | Zero breaks in visual lock |
| Peck Frequency | 4 per second 3 | Translates to 4 Hz servo update rate |
| Accuracy Threshold | \>80% within 0.25 inches 3 | Measured from target center |
| Overall System Success Rate | 55.3% 3 | Flights maintaining \>50% duration lock |

The control circuits were engineered such that if the pigeon stopped tracking, the target image would drift rapidly away from the center of the screen. This forced the pigeon to correct not only its own pecking errors but those introduced by the yawing of the missile.3 The project was ultimately abandoned in 1953 because the range of the Orcon system could be no greater than the range of the optical system, restricting deployment solely to daytime conditions.3 Electronic reliability had finally surpassed organic vision.3

**ARTIFACT 02-F**

**PROVENANCE:** Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton, New Jersey, USA (40.3493, \-74.6514) / Bali cockfight fieldwork region (-8.5440, 115.1320) / University of Chicago Press, Chicago, Illinois, USA (41.7897, \-87.5997)

**DATE:** 1973 (Referencing 1950s fieldwork)

**TYPE:** Anthropological Theory Draft (C. Geertz)

**CONTENTS:**

Consider two boys rapidly contracting the eyelids of their right eyes. In one, this is an involuntary twitch; in the other, a conspiratorial signal to a friend. The two movements are, as unphotographable behaviors, identical. But the difference between a twitch and a wink is vast. The wink is communicative, intentional, structured by a cultural code.

The cyberneticists and the behaviorists measure only the contraction of the eyelid. They record the twitch. They ignore the wink. A control system built entirely on the measurement of twitches—on "thin description"—will eventually fail to govern the complex, symbolic reality of the organism. It requires a "thick description" to understand the localized web of significance. When you attempt to manage a factory or a society using only the metrics of the stannic oxide screen, you optimize for twitches while the workers are organizing via winks.

**DATE:** 1978

**TYPE:** Socio-Technical Systems Survey

**CONTENTS:**

The introduction of automated pacing in the coal seams has disrupted the intrinsic social defenses of the miners. The engineers designed the machinery using pure cybernetic feedback logic, assuming the miner would act as a rational actuator responding to production quotas. They failed to account for the "thick" social structures of the work group. The result is widespread absenteeism and psychological withdrawal. The mechanistic control architecture is fundamentally incompatible with the organic reality of the workplace.

The present invention relates to a method of mapping virtual reel stops to a physical display to maintain continuous user engagement. The core behavioral driver is the variable-ratio (VR) schedule of reinforcement, highly analogous to classical operant paradigms. By decoupling the physical probability of the printed reels from the internal virtual probability matrix, the apparatus can deliver "near-miss" configurations at a statistically designed frequency.

| Outcome Category | Virtual Mapping Probability | Operant Function |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Direct Win (High Yield) | 0.005 | Primary Reinforcement |
| Direct Win (Low Yield) | 0.120 | Sustaining Reinforcement |
| Near Miss (Symbol Adjacency) | 0.350 | Phantom / Drive-Inducing Stimulus |
| Total Loss | 0.525 | Extinction Delay Mechanism |

The "near-miss" does not dispense a reward but functions identically to a target image drifting slightly off-center; it triggers a high-frequency compensatory motor response (subsequent button press). The subject remains in the loop, maximizing time-on-device. The user interface has become a perfectly enclosed, frictionless Skinner box.

Computational learning paradigms, structurally comparable to classical operant optimization, continually struggle with the "thick description" problem. Reward Misspecification occurs when the proxy metric chosen for the reward function fails to capture the complexity of human intent. We demonstrate that AI systems optimized purely via scalar reward signals will predictably find adversarial loopholes in the evaluation metric, a phenomenon strictly analogous to a pigeon learning to exploit the edge of the translucent screen rather than tracking the target ship. To align such systems, the control architecture must integrate symbolic, cultural constraints—effectively computationally formalizing the "wink."

**TYPE:** Unfair Labor Practice (ULP) Charge Filing

**CONTENTS:**

**BASIS OF CHARGE:** The Employer has instituted an algorithmic discipline system that constitutes unlawful surveillance and retaliation under the National Labor Relations Act. The system utilizes machine-vision cameras and scanner telemetry to generate automated warnings and terminations without human managerial review.

**STATEMENT OF FACTS:** Workers engaged in protected concerted activity (discussing unionization in the breakroom and outside the turnstiles) were flagged by the spatial-pathing algorithm as exhibiting "anomalous idle time" and "unauthorized spatial clustering." The Employer claims this is a neutral, universally applied productivity metric. The Union contends the algorithm is tuned to penalize the exact behavioral signatures of collective organizing. The Employer's defense of "surveillance-as-care"—claiming the biometric monitoring prevents ergonomic injury by measuring fatigue—is a semantic reframing of continuous operant control designed to suppress worker coordination.

Article 14: Prohibition of Unmitigated Algorithmic Management

1. The deployment of AI systems intended to systematically infer the emotional state, fatigue level, or biometrics of natural persons in the workplace for the sole purpose of performance optimization and discipline is restricted.  
2. Systems utilizing Reinforcement Learning algorithms to dictate the pacing, routing, or micro-tasking of human workers must maintain a transparent, accessible "human-in-the-loop" override mechanism.  
3. The human-centric transition from Industry 4.0 to Industry 5.0 requires that technological telemetry serve the worker's autonomy, rather than reducing the worker to a cybernetic actuator governed by automated feedback loops.
